title: Hourly to Annual Pay: National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates and Salary Sacrifice Charity Options
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. Compare the National Minimum Wage with award rates, casual loading, and super. Learn how salary sacrifice
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour yields an annual gross salary of approximately $52,249.28 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, super, and any deductions. Remember that this assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum pay for employees not covered by an award or agreement, set by the Fair Work Commission. As of 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week. Award rates are minimum wages set for specific industries or occupations, often higher than the National Minimum Wage. They also include penalty rates, allowances, and casual loadings. Always check your relevant award or enterprise agreement, as your minimum pay may be higher than the national minimum.

faqs.q: How does salary sacrifice to charity affect my take-home pay?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice to charity involves directing part of your pre-tax salary to a registered charity, reducing your taxable income. This can lower the tax you pay and increase your take-home pay compared to donating after tax. However, salary sacrifice arrangements are subject to rules from the Australian Taxation Office and your employer's policy. Our calculator does not include salary sacrifice, so you should adjust your estimates accordingly. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Pay

Whether you're negotiating a salary, comparing job offers, or planning your budget, converting your hourly rate to an annual figure is a fundamental step. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week, as this is the standard ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the hours accordingly. For example, a 20-hour week would use 20 instead of 38.

### Why 38 Hours and 52 Weeks?

The 38-hour week is the benchmark for full-time employment in Australia. It comes from the National Employment Standards. Multiplying by 52 weeks gives a full-year figure, though many people take unpaid leave or have variable hours. This estimate assumes you work every week of the year at the same rate, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To get your gross fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly pay. Using the formula: hourly rate × 38 × 2 = fortnightly gross. For the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, that's $26.44 × 38 × 2 = $2,009.44 per fortnight before tax and super.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The **National Minimum Wage** is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

However, most employees are covered by an **award** – a legal document that sets minimum pay and conditions for a specific industry or job. Award rates are almost always higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, a retail employee under the General Retail Industry Award may earn more than $26.44 per hour depending on their classification and experience. Always check your award or enterprise agreement on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

If you are not covered by an award or agreement, the National Minimum Wage applies. Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details on current rates.

### Casual Loading and Super

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. This loading is included in the casual rate shown on our [the timesheet](/) – simply tick the 'casual loading' checkbox. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading**; the tool adds it automatically.

Superannuation (super) is paid on top of your gross wages. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for 38 hours, your employer contributes an extra $26.44 × 38 × 52 × 12% = $6,269.91 per year into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay – it's an additional benefit.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (generally). The tax-free threshold is included. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator estimates your net pay after tax and Medicare, but does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Salary Sacrifice Charity and Tax

One way to reduce your taxable income is through **salary sacrifice charity** arrangements. Under these, you agree to forgo part of your pre-tax salary, which your employer pays directly to a registered charity. This lowers your assessable income, potentially reducing the tax you pay. For example, if you earn $80,000 and salary sacrifice $5,000 to charity, your taxable income drops to $75,000, saving you tax at your marginal rate. However, salary sacrifice is subject to employer policy and ATO rules. Our calculator does not include any salary sacrifice, so you should adjust your estimates manually if you use this strategy.

## Average Earnings in Australia

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) data. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week. That's an annual equivalent of about $108,352.40. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or $82,118.40 per year. These are averages across all industries and states, not a median for any specific job. For more context, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

## Using Our Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates annual, weekly, fortnightly, and monthly gross pay, plus estimated tax, Medicare, and super. Remember the disclaimer: this is an estimate only. It assumes consistent hours, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings up to the cap. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed.

For more detailed information on specific pay topics, explore our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data).
